summary: OFAC says PARECO-FF controlled Rubaya mining sites from 2022 to early 2024, collecting fees and taxes. End date set to the eve of the M23 takeover.
UN experts: the Rubaya sites stayed under PARECO-FF, which oversaw extraction, with Rubaya hill and D2 Bibatama active in January 2024.
UN experts: AFC/M23 has held Rubaya town and the whole surrounding mining area since 30 April 2024.
UN experts list the sites M23 worked inside PE76 and revoked PE4731, and the trading centres it held.
UN experts: mining around Rubaya stayed under AFC/M23 and rose; output is assessed above 120 t a month from March 2026 satellite imagery.
Amnesty: M23 holds exclusive control of the mine and much of the surrounding area, despite attacks by other armed groups. Observed date is approximate: last interviews cited are May 2026.
OFAC refers to Rubaya as an M23-controlled mine at the March 2026 collapse.
UN experts: M23 taxed coltan and manganese at $7/kg and cassiterite at $4/kg, raising at least $800,000 a month.
UN experts: M23 still taxes all actors, now about $4/kg coltan and $2/kg cassiterite at sale, with licences and a daily access fee.
UN experts: mining sites in the Rubaya area were under PARECO-FF until the M23 takeover.
